quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: Bad suspension in your car can cause:

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Slack in the steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Suspension helps you control your vehicle and provides a smooth ride. If your vehicle bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long periods.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.
No turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed. Do not turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. You must:

options.text: Have done as much as you can.
Stay until the police arrive.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.
Leave and continue on your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.question: If your view is blocked at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach an intersection. If you cannot see clearly, stop completely. Then move forward slowly until you can see traffic in both directions.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol may affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and coordination, even below the legal limit. Drinking and driving is dangerous and illegal.

questions.question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind on a hill, you should know:

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often go slower than the speed limit, especially uphill. On a hill with poor visibility, it is illegal to pass. Be careful approaching trucks from behind.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible driving speeds for the area.
The highest and lowest speeds you are legally allowed to drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in poor conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest and lowest speeds you are legally allowed to drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the legal maximum and minimum speeds for that road. Speed limits are for ideal conditions. You must slow down when weather or traffic conditions require it.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by:

options.text: Driving through shallow water.
Driving faster.
Driving slower.
Driving through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is moving faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your rearview mirror.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway. This helps you spot vehicles and merge safely.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived before you. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on the car.

questions.question: This white sign means:

options.text: The crossing is controlled. Keep driving at your normal speed.
Look and listen. Be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look and listen. Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, look and listen. Slow down and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you go.

questions.question: You cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Which statement is true about large trucks?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than regular cars.
They all have air brakes that stop quickly.
They are easier to steer than regular cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than regular cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. A truck at 55 mph may need 800 feet to stop, while a car needs only 400 feet.

questions.question: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest speed allowed under good conditions. You must slow down when the road is slippery or when visibility is poor.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You cannot stop your vehicle there at any time.
You can park there if the driver stays in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only stop temporarily to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs about upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on white background
Black letters or symbols on yellow background
White letters or symbols on blue background
White letters or symbols on green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs have black letters or symbols on a yellow background. Work zone warning signs have black letters or symbols on an orange background.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles with trailers may not see you behind them. Increase your following distance behind these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so stay farther back to see around them.

questions.question: What does a single broken white centerline mean?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You can cross it to change lanes.
You can change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross it to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines show lanes going the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet appears. These conditions make roads slippery. When road conditions are poor, you may need to drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety.
